B.explanation: Starts at $0$ and moves downward first, then oscillates with period $T$ for two cycles to $2T$.

walkthrough: At $t=0$ particle X is on the dashed equilibrium line, so its displacement $y=0$. The required $y-t$ graph must therefore start at the origin.
For a wave moving to the right with speed $v$, the particle velocity is opposite in sign to the wave slope. At X the rope slopes upward to the right from trough toward crest.
An upward slope with rightward wave motion means the particle moves downward next. Imagine the whole pattern shifting right a little: the trough moves toward X, pulling X below equilibrium.
So the $y-t$ graph starts at $0$ with negative gradient - going into negative displacement first.
Particle X then performs simple harmonic motion with period $T$. Between $0$ and $2T$ it completes two full oscillations, returning to $0$ at $t=T$ and $t=2T$.
Only the graph that starts at $0$, goes negative first, and shows two cycles fits this. This is option B.
